chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Zyad, from Mansoor, from Nasr al-Kowsaj, from Mutrif - a servant of Ma'an, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The sweetness of belief will not enter the heart of a Sindhi, a Zanji, nor a Khuzestani, nor a Kurd, nor a Berber, nor a Nabak of Ray, and nor one whose mother carried him in adultery.

key_terms.نَبَكِ الرِّيِّ: Nabak of Ray (a specific tribe/region in Ray)

ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people whose hearts will not taste the sweetness of faith according to Imam Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies seven specific categories—defined by regional, ethnic, or genealogical markers such as Sindhi, Zanji, and those born of adultery—who will not taste the sweetness of faith. While often interpreted as referring to specific historical groups or traits associated with them, Shia scholars note that this is not necessarily an absolute exclusion but rather a description of their spiritual state or a reference to the 'seven hearts' mentioned in related traditions. This highlights the interplay between lineage, geography, and spiritual receptivity in Shia theological discourse.
